section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection between the three pilgrimage festivals and the times of grain ripening, describing the spiritual growth that results from the descent of souls into physical bodies and exile, culminating in future revelation.
section.t: Now, it is explained in the discourses
the connection of the three pilgrimage festivals to the times of the ripening of the grains,
for then
(on the three pilgrimage festivals)
is the growth of the spiritual grain that comes through the sowing.
And the concept is,
as it is written,
"And I will sow her for Me in the land,"
and it is known
that this refers to the descent of the souls
(the spiritual grain)
below to be clothed in a body and an animal soul
(land),
and more specifically, to the descent of the exile.
For the intention in this is for the sake of ascent,
similar to sowing in the earth
(in its simple sense)
which is for the sake of growth in greater multiplicity than was initially.
And the growth
(the ascent)
is through the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos, which is also called by the name "sowing."
In addition to the sowing of the descent of the soul below
(that the Holy One, blessed be He, brought the soul down below),
there must also be the work of sowing by Israel,
the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos.
For through the souls descending below,
and especially in the time of exile,
and nevertheless they fulfill Torah and mitzvos
(in a manner of subjugation and transformation),
through this the growth is effected—the drawing down of a revelation incomparably higher than the revelation that the soul had before its descent below.
And the main revelation of the growth will be in the future to come.
And an illumination from this shines even now,
on the three pilgrimage festivals.
On the first festival
(the Festival of Matzos)
which is the growth of the ripening of barley,
it is the matter of fear,
which is the first gate
through which one enters to cling to Him, blessed be He.
And this is that "se'orah" (barley) is the letters of "sha'ar HaShem" (the gate of HaShem),
"sha'ar" is from the term "gate" and the "hei" is the lower hei
(Malchus).
And on the second festival
(the Festival of Shavuos)
is the growth of wheat, which is human food,
it is the Torah, of which it is written,
"This is the Torah, a man."
And this is that "chitah" (wheat) has the numerical value of twenty-two, hinting at the twenty-two letters of the Torah.
And it is explained in the aforementioned discourses,
that this is the connection of Atzeres to the fruits of the tree
(Atzeres regarding the fruits of the tree),
for wheat is a type of tree
(according to one opinion),
which hints at man, as it is written, "For man is the tree of the field,"
and on Shavuos
(Atzeres)
the Torah was given,
"This is the Torah, a man."
And it can be said,
that since that wheat is a type of tree is only according to one opinion,
and even according to this opinion it is only a type of tree,
therefore the matter of the Torah hinted at in wheat is the level of Torah as it relates to mitzvos.
And the Torah itself, which is above the matter of mitzvos,
the essential matter of "man"
("This is the Torah, a man"),
is hinted at in the fruits of the tree.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos is called "sowing" for two reasons: it refines the body and animal soul, and it involves self-nullification through accepting the yoke of Heaven, especially during exile.
section.t: And the concept is,
that this that the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos is called by the name "sowing" is from two aspects.
Because through the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos, the refinement of the body and the animal soul is effected,
and through this the root of the body and animal soul is revealed, which is above the root of the G-dly soul—similar to sowing in its simple sense,
that through sowing the grain and the seed in the earth, the growing power within the earth is aroused and revealed.
And also,
because the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos must be
(not because of the reason, but rather)
in order to fulfill the command of the Holy One, blessed be He,
as per the wording in the blessing over mitzvos, "Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us,"
the self-nullification of acceptance of the yoke—similar to sowing in its simple sense,
that the rooting of the seed in the earth is through the rotting of the seed.
And this is the reason that the main growth is through the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos in the time of exile,
for in the time of the Holy Temple,
when there was a revelation of G-dliness
(including also the revelation through the fulfillment of mitzvos),
the self-nullification of acceptance of the yoke was not so felt,
since the revelation through the mitzvos was then felt.
And the main self-nullification of acceptance of the yoke is in the time of exile,
and especially in the generation of the heels of Mashiach,
to the extent that the fulfillment of mitzvos then is in a manner of "those who sow in tears,"
and specifically through this, "with joy they will reap."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between Torah and mitzvos, explaining that mitzvos involve refinement and self-nullification of the person, while Torah is G-d's wisdom itself, with which one unifies through study, transcending the level of a servant.
section.t: Now, it is known
the distinction between Torah and mitzvos,
that mitzvos are commands to man,
and Torah is the word of HaShem,
the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,
except that it descended below and became clothed in human intellect.
From this it is understood,
that the two matters mentioned above regarding sowing
(the refinement of the body and animal soul, and the self-nullification of acceptance of the yoke)
are primarily in the fulfillment of mitzvos,
unlike Torah.
For in mitzvos, which are commands to man,
it is applicable to say that their intention is to refine the creations through them,

for the sake of the refinement and purification of the body and animal soul of the person who performs the mitzvah, and for the sake of the refinement and purification of the things in the world with which the mitzvah is performed.
But unlike Torah, which is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,
it is not applicable to say that it is a means, heaven forbid, to effect something in man and in the world.
And the effect that is brought about through it in the person who studies it,
is,
that through his study of Torah, the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is above the world, is drawn into him
[and the drawing of Torah into the person who studies it is in a manner that he becomes unified with it].
And similarly regarding the self-nullification of acceptance of the yoke
(the second matter of sowing),
in mitzvos, which are commands to man
(which indicates that in the level of mitzvos, man has a place of grasp),
man is an existence.
And that he fulfills the command is from the aspect of self-nullification of acceptance of the yoke,
like a servant
who fulfills the command of the king.
And in Torah, which is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,
there is no place given to an existence outside of Him,
not even to the existence of a servant,
and therefore the perfection of engaging in Torah is when his study is in a manner that the word of HaShem speaks from his mouth.
And this is what our sages said,
"Who are the kings? The Rabbis,"
for their study of Torah is in a manner that the word of HaShem speaks through them,
and therefore they are in ultimate self-nullification, above even the self-nullification of a servant,
to the extent that their entire existence is the King Himself,
for through Torah, Israel and the Holy One, blessed be He, are all one.
And even one who is not on this level, that his study of Torah would be in this manner that the word of HaShem speaks from his mouth,
nevertheless,
the main emphasis in engaging in Torah is not on the matter of self-nullification and subjugation,
but rather, on the contrary,
on this—that his existence
(his understanding and comprehension)
should be one with the Torah.
